name: Cranberry Wine
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: water to 2 quarts of berries
ingredients.originalText: 1 quart of water to 2 quarts of berries

ingredients.name: sugar for 3 quarts of liquor
ingredients.originalText: 1 lb. sugar for 3 quarts of liquor

instructions.text: Mash ripe berries to a pulp; put into a stone jar
Stir well and let it stand two days
Strain through a double flannel bag
Mash a second supply of berries, equal in quantity to the first, and cover with this liquid
Let it ferment in lightly covered jars

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Mash ripe berries to a pulp; put into a stone jar
2. Add water
3. Stir well and let it stand two days
4. Strain through a double flannel bag
5. Mash a second supply of berries, equal in quantity to the first, and cover with this liquid
6. Steep two days more
7. Strain and add sugar
8. Boil five minutes
9. Let it ferment in lightly covered jars
10. Rack off and bottle
originalIngredients: 1 quart of water to 2 quarts of berries
1 lb. sugar for 3 quarts of liquor
